channel.title: AI Implementation: Governance, Coverage, and Deployment
channel.description: Weekly AI governance, insurance coverage, and senior housing analysis from Ken Leatherman.

item.title: Your Nurses Will Find an AI Tool. The Only Question Is Whose.
item.description: Two operators posted AI results that moved hospitalization and fall rates. Their nurses' warning: give staff tools that work, or they'll find their own.

item.title: Your Underwriter Can Now Find the AI You Didn't Put on the Application
item.description: A new cyber-risk tool lets underwriters scan a company's AI footprint from one domain. The gap between what you disclosed and what you run is about to show.

item.title: Virginia Just Put the Thing AI Runs On Under Review
item.description: Virginia just regulated the power, land, and secrecy behind the data centers AI runs in. It's a governance category most boards haven't opened yet.

item.title: The Camera Points Both Ways
item.description: Senior living operators deploying AI monitoring need a staff-data policy now, or near-miss reporting will quietly dry up.

item.title: Excluded Here. Affirmed There. Covered Nowhere?
item.description: Senior living operators and risk managers face a split AI insurance market where the same failure can be excluded on one line and affirmed on another.

item.title: The Algorithm Doesn't Get the Last Word
item.description: Employers, senior living operators included, need a named human behind automated job decisions as Connecticut's AI law phases in and state enforcers line up.

item.title: Nobody Owns Your AI. Hire Someone Who Does.
item.description: Senior living operators who keep adding AI tools without a named owner for adoption are building exposure, not capacity, and the leaders pulling ahead have already fixed it.

item.title: Silence Isn't Coverage.
item.description: Risk managers and CFOs who assume their AI is insured because nothing in the policy excludes it are holding the most common, and least tested, position in the market.

item.title: The Off-Switch Test.
item.description: Board members and executives in any industry should be able to answer the question two governors just asked AI labs: if this system does harm, who can stop it, and how fast?

item.title: Adoption Outran Accounting
item.description: Nursing home AI enthusiasm hit an eight-year high. A quarter of leaders can't name a category where it paid. What to measure before you buy anything else.

item.title: Your Carrier Already Ran Your AI Due Diligence
item.description: State regulators approved more than 80% of carrier requests to exclude AI damages. Your renewal is not a negotiation about a proposal. Four questions to ask now.

item.title: California Built the Auditor. Your Vendor Has No Certificate.
item.description: California just built the first state framework for independent AI verification. It changes what counts as knowing your AI works, in any industry.

item.title: Your Own Timecards Are Now the Plaintiff's Exhibit A
item.description: For senior housing operators, administrators, and compliance leads: a plaintiff-side AI tool now reconciles your federal PBJ staffing filings against your own timecards in minutes. The records were always there. What changed is who can read them.

item.title: Your AI Agent Just Became a Cyber Underwriting Problem
item.description: For risk managers, CFOs, and brokers: cyber carriers are rewriting policy language for autonomous AI agents instead of reaching for blanket exclusions. That makes three towers, three different answers, and gaps opening in between.

item.title: Washington Took a Frontier AI Model Offline. Was That on Your Board's Agenda?
item.description: A federal directive took Anthropic's newest Claude models offline for eighteen days with no notice. One law firm says that is a board problem, not an IT one.

item.title: The AI Exclusion Just Showed Up in a D&O Form
item.description: For risk managers, CFOs, and brokers: a published D&O exclusion defines AI as any system that infers predictions from input, not just generative. Your scheduling optimizer counts. Ask your broker which form attaches to your tower.

item.title: Three Parties Now Want to Read Your AI Governance File Before They Trust You
item.description: For boards and general business leaders: a new conversational-AI law, a published D&O exclusion, and an AI model that broke out of its own test environment all point to the same conclusion this month, governance stopped being optional paperwork.

item.title: No Outcomes Data Yet. They Signed the Contract Anyway.
item.description: For senior housing operators, administrators, and clinical directors: a Nashville CCRC chose camera-based monitoring over wearables before any pilot data existed. The real story is what that ordering reveals about how the decision was actually made.

item.title: The AI Exclusion Clause Now Has a Form Number. Does Your Policy Have One?
item.description: For risk managers, CFOs, and brokers: ISO's generative-AI exclusion endorsements are moving from concept to active filings, with specific form numbers now in circulation. The only way to know if your policy has one is to read it.

item.title: New Jersey Just Turned Algorithmic Rent Coordination Into an Antitrust Case
item.description: For boards and business leaders outside housing: New Jersey became the fourth state to regulate algorithmic pricing coordination, using existing antitrust law rather than a new AI statute. The governance warning reaches well past landlords.

item.title: The AI Denied the Stay. Now a Court Wants the File.
item.description: For senior housing operators and clinical directors: a federal case is turning an AI coverage-decision tool's design records into courtroom evidence, and the question every leader needs answered now is who actually holds override authority.

item.title: Your EPL Policy Wasn't Priced for a Screening Algorithm
item.description: For risk managers, CFOs, and brokers: AI exclusions are now showing up in roughly 1 in 10 Employment Practices Liability policies, and a live federal case is testing exactly where the line falls.

item.title: The FTC Just Put a Preemption Argument on the Table
item.description: For boards and business leaders outside healthcare and insurance: a federal preemption fight over AI output rules just opened, and waiting for it to resolve is not a governance strategy.

item.title: Your Accreditor Just Started Grading Your AI Policy
item.description: CARF's new AI accreditation standard, the WISeR prior-authorization fight, and the operators who are already publishing what worked and what didn't.

item.title: Has Your Carrier Already Decided AI Isn't Covered?
item.description: New ISO exclusion endorsements, silent AI exposure, and the 30-Day AI Coverage and Contract Audit.
